long_biography.plain_text:
A bicycle gave Duncan Bannatyne his first lesson in enterprise. Raised in modest circumstances in Clydebank, he persuaded a newsagent to create a paper round. After finding one hundred customers, he used the earnings to buy the bicycle his family could not afford. Years later, he bought an ice-cream van, expanded the fleet and sold the business to finance a move into residential care.

Quality Care Homes and the Just Learning nursery chain provided two major exits before Bannatyne concentrated on health clubs, spas and hotels. He remains a director and controlling shareholder of the Bannatyne Group, whose health clubs form its principal business. Television made him widely known as a Dragons' Den investor, while charitable work brought him an OBE.
